title: Modular monolith — spoken follow-up
situation: In a technical discussion, an interviewer asks why the project has one deployable unit. You must answer aloud accurately without overstating the evidence.
instructions: Say aloud why the project ships as one deployable unit, and name the condition that would justify splitting it.

vocabulary.meaning: the reasoning that ties a structural choice to a constraint, rather than to a trend
a separation enforced inside one deployable unit, which keeps the option of splitting later without paying for it now

expectedElements: The single unit is defended by a constraint, not by taste
A condition that would justify splitting is named
modelAnswer: One deployable unit, and that is a constraint-driven choice rather than a preference. We are a small team with no platform engineers, so every additional deployable is our operational cost, not somebody else's. Inside the unit the modules are separated: each owns its data, and calls cross module boundaries through an explicit interface, not through a shared table. That means the option of splitting later stays open and we are not paying for it now. What would justify splitting is evidence that one module needs to scale or to be released independently of the rest, and neither is true today. Do you see that changing?
commonMistakes: Defending the single unit as simpler without naming the constraint behind it
Claiming modularity without describing what enforces the boundaries
variants: Answer again to an interviewer who considers this an outdated choice.
